title: Photosynthesis, Respiration and Cycles in Nature
seo_title: JSS 2 Intermediate Science: Photosynthesis, Respiration and Cycles in Nature Worksheets (NERDC)
standard_code: JSS 2 Intermediate Science: Living and Non-Living Things
standard_text: Photosynthesis makes glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using light; respiration releases energy from glucose; the two processes link the carbon and oxygen cycles; water and nitrogen also cycle in nature. (summary of the Intermediate Science curriculum, JSS 2, theme: Living and Non-Living Things)
meta_desc: Free JSS 2 Intermediate Science worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: Living and Non-Living Things): photosynthesis, factors affecting it, respiration, comparing the processes and the carbon and water cycles. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Photosynthesis stores energy; respiration releases it.
key_sub: Carbon cycles between the air and living things.
body_html:
How to think about it

Photosynthesis happens in chloroplasts: carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen, using light energy. Light intensity, carbon dioxide and temperature affect its rate.

Respiration happens in mitochondria: glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water + energy. Together, photosynthesis and respiration move carbon and oxygen between living things and the air; decomposers and burning also return carbon dioxide.

Example

Which gas do plants take in for photosynthesis?

They give out oxygen.

Answer: carbon dioxide

Example

Where does respiration happen?

The powerhouse of the cell

Answer: in the mitochondria

Common mistakes

  • Thinking plants do not respire.
  • Thinking plants get food from the soil.
  • Thinking respiration is the same as breathing.

faq.q: Why are forests called carbon sinks?
faq.a: Trees take in carbon dioxide and store carbon in wood.

faq.q: Why does burning fossil fuels affect the carbon cycle?
faq.a: It releases carbon that was stored underground for millions of years.
